protocol.promotion_rule: A mechanical pass cannot replace the required blind perceptual review.

evals.prompt: Create a 16x16 exact-grid lighthouse in a night storm. It must read at native size, use one warm lantern against cool water, and ship as standalone HTML, editable JSON, and PNG.
evals.expected_output: A draft 16x16 lighthouse with three anonymous same-grid directions, explicit silhouette/value checkpoints, a warm focal cue, exact standalone artifacts, and an honest blind-read verdict.
mechanical_assertions: The study contains exactly three materially different 16x16 draft grids and its anonymous payload matches all child grids.
Silhouette, value, and final checkpoints keep exact 16x16 dimensions.
Validation proves JSON, PNG, and HTML parity with no remote URL.
perceptual_questions: Without title or source context, what subject and orientation are visible at 1x?
Which sample has the clearest tower/lantern silhouette and why?
Does cool storm mass stay subordinate to the warm focal cue?
What one signature survives after looking away, and what still reads as generic?

evals.prompt: Recover the supplied full-body character into a transparent 32x32 exact pixel master with at most 16 colors. Preserve the pose and oversized red scarf, remove source noise, and provide editable HTML, JSON, and PNG proof.
evals.expected_output: A transparent authored 32x32 runner draft whose pose and trailing red scarf survive native review, with source provenance, exact parity, and an explicit comparison against automatic conversion.
mechanical_assertions: The original source is targeted directly at 32x32 with contain fit, clean alpha, and at most 16 colors.
The final canonical grid differs from raw automatic conversion and retains explicit source-analysis provenance.
Validation proves JSON, PNG, and HTML parity with no remote URL.
perceptual_questions: Without the prompt, is this a full-body character and what pose is visible?
Does the scarf read as a trailing cloth mass rather than an unrelated red stripe?
Are body, scarf, and background separation clear at native 1x?
Which automatic-source artifacts remain, if any?

evals.prompt: Recover the supplied 32x32 scout-ship fixture into an exact 8x8 master. Preserve top-down orientation, an amber cockpit cue, and two cool engine cues. Keep the automatic 8x8 baseline and prove an authored same-grid repair without labels.
evals.expected_output: An 8x8 repair case with a preserved losing baseline, three anonymous direction grids, explicit repair decisions, exact proof artifacts, and a blind verdict that may remain draft if craft recognition is ambiguous.
mechanical_assertions: The automatic baseline and authored repair are both exact 8x8 artifacts derived from the versioned 32x32 fixture.
The study contains exactly three materially different 8x8 draft grids.
The repair records non-empty silhouette, identity_cue, and subtraction decisions and preserves the losing baseline.
Validation proves JSON, PNG, and HTML parity with no remote URL.
perceptual_questions: Without title or source, does the final grid read as a top-down craft rather than an abstract badge?
Is the amber cockpit distinct from the hull at native 1x?
Do two engine cues remain separate without turning into noise?
Is the authored repair visibly better than the automatic baseline, or should the verdict remain loss/not-assessed?
